title: The 'How Long' solo with Jimmy Rushing
summary: Morgenstern praises Price's solo records; Price recalls the 'How Long' track and a dedication.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I notice in that list of yours there are not too many piano solos. You made a lot of solo records. No, what I was saying was that I didn't notice too many piano solos on that list of yours.

Well, I'm modest enough, Dan, not to, you know, I'm modest enough not to...I've got that much sense. I'm not bragging on myself. If some guy, though...if somebody else don't write about my piano playing, then, you know, far be it from me. I could, but I won't. I won't pass judgment on myself.
I would add one or...start from some of the solo things which I think are beautiful. You remember the "How Long, How Long" That you did with Jimmy Rushing...

Man. But again, nobody ever came up to me and said, "Man, that was really nice." I said it on the record, at the end of the record, if you let it play long enough, and you have the volume up, you'll see...I say, "Man, that's a bitch." That's on that record, you know, way...before it reject. If you just let it play that part before it reject you'll hear that. See..oh, that was something.
That was dedicated to Liz, wasn't it?
Yeah...but I, you know, I guess you can't wave your own horn...wave your own flag, or can you?
You worked a lot with Sidney Bechet.. You hear different versions about Sidney Bechet. Was he that difficult to get along with?
No. He was just...he was a thorough musician. Just a thorough musician and wasn't to be played with. And he wasn't to be, you know...he was ready to go to the war in a minute.
